title: GPU capability detection + normalization for selector v2 (SKU mapping, SM capability, MIG/partitioning)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
## Context
Kernel auto-selection v2 needs a stable, low-cardinality GPU identifier to select kernels by GPU class/SKU + SM capability. Today we have a mix of heuristics (string matching `cudaGetDeviceProperties().name`, implicit assumptions from device memory size, etc.) that are:
- inconsistent across cloud providers / driver versions
- brittle for new SKUs (L4 variants, H100 PCIe vs SXM, etc.)
- incorrect/unstable under MIG and other partitioned environments (reported names change; memory size reflects partition)

This ticket adds a single normalization layer that produces **canonical GPU capability + normalized SKU class** for use by selector v2 and telemetry.

## Goals
- Produce a canonical, deterministic GPU identity from runtime signals:
  - SKU class: `L4 | A10 | A100 | H100 | Unknown`
  - SM capability: `sm_75 / sm_80 / sm_86 / sm_89 / sm_90` (etc.)
  - Partitioning context: MIG enabled + MIG profile when available
- Make the output stable across:
  - driver updates (minor name formatting changes)
  - container/runtime environments (K8s, systemd, bare metal)
  - MIG configurations (1g/2g/3g/4g/7g profiles)
- Provide safe fallback behavior: if we can’t determine a known SKU class, return `Unknown` and force selector v2 to route to “safe kernel set” (or v1 fallback depending on selector config).

## Non-goals
- Full GPU inventory management (this is per-process local detection).
- Detecting every GPU SKU under the sun; we target the Redwood fleet matrix first (L4, A10, A100, H100) and add a correct unknown path.

## Proposed output contract (used by selector v2)
The normalization layer returns a single structure (conceptually) with:
- `gpu_vendor`: `nvidia`
- `gpu_sku_class`: one of `L4/A10/A100/H100/Unknown`
- `gpu_sm`: `sm_<major><minor>` derived from compute capability
- `gpu_mem_gb_bucket`: coarse memory bucket for debugging only (e.g., `<=16`, `<=24`, `<=40`, `<=80`, `>80`) to avoid high-cardinality
- `gpu_is_mig`: `true/false`
- `gpu_mig_profile`: coarse profile name when available (e.g., `1g.5gb`, `2g.10gb`, `3g.20gb`, `7g.80gb`, else `unknown`)

Notes:
- Selector should key off `gpu_sku_class` + `gpu_sm` + `gpu_is_mig` (and optionally profile) only.
- Telemetry should NOT include raw device names or UUIDs.

## Detection strategy
1) Prefer NVML when available (more accurate for MIG):
   - Identify physical GPU vs MIG device
   - Get compute capability / arch
   - Get MIG mode + profile (when running on MIG instance)
2) Fall back to CUDA runtime properties if NVML is unavailable:
   - Use `cudaDeviceProp.major/minor` for compute capability
   - Use `cudaDeviceProp.name` with pattern mapping to `gpu_sku_class`
   - Detect “MIG-ish” names and mark `gpu_is_mig=true` but treat profile as `unknown` unless confidently parsed

## SKU normalization rules (initial)
- H100:
  - compute capability `9.0` => `gpu_sm=sm_90`
  - names matching `H100` => `gpu_sku_class=H100`
- A100:
  - compute capability `8.0` => `gpu_sm=sm_80`
  - names matching `A100` => `gpu_sku_class=A100`
- L4:
  - compute capability `8.9` => `gpu_sm=sm_89`
  - names matching `L4` => `gpu_sku_class=L4`
- A10:
  - compute capability `8.6` => `gpu_sm=sm_86`
  - names matching `A10` => `gpu_sku_class=A10`
- Unknown:
  - otherwise, `gpu_sku_class=Unknown` and selector v2 must not attempt “aggressive” kernels.

Important: compute capability alone is NOT sufficient to distinguish all SKUs; we still use name matching, but it is centralized and versioned.

## MIG/partitioned environments
- MIG detection:
  - NVML: if device is a MIG device or MIG mode enabled and a MIG instance is visible to the process
  - CUDA-only: parse device name patterns containing `MIG` and set `gpu_is_mig=true`
- Policy for selector v2:
  - When `gpu_is_mig=true`, default to the conservative kernel choices for the `gpu_sku_class` unless registry has an explicit MIG entry.
  - Reason: MIG memory + SM partitioning shifts optimal kernels, and we’ve seen tail-latency variance when treating MIG as full device.

## Implementation plan
- Add a `gpu_caps` module in runtime:
  - single public function: `DetectAndNormalizeGpuCaps()` (name TBD)
  - returns normalized fields used by selector context
- Add unit tests:
  - fixtures for common `cudaDeviceProp.name` strings seen in fleet
  - fixtures for NVML MIG profiles
  - regression test: ensure deterministic output for the same inputs
- Wire into selector v2 context:
  - replace existing scattered detection code paths
  - ensure selection telemetry uses normalized fields

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Selector v2 context includes `gpu_sku_class` and `gpu_sm` from the normalization layer.
- [x] MIG is detected reliably in our K8s MIG clusters; `gpu_is_mig=true` when running inside MIG.
- [x] Unknown GPU does not crash and forces safe selection path (either v1 fallback or safe kernel set).
- [x] Telemetry labels are low-cardinality (no raw UUID, no raw device name).
- [x] Tests cover at least: L4, A10, A100 (40/80), H100, and one unknown.

## Rollout / risk
- Low functional risk but high blast radius if wrong: misclassification can pick the wrong kernel and regress tail latency.
- Mitigation:
  - keep selector v2 feature-flagged
  - add debug endpoint output (ENG-3932) to print normalized GPU caps
  - dashboards should break down by `gpu_sku_class` (not raw)

## Follow-ups (out of scope here)
- Add explicit MIG entries to kernel registry once we have benchmark coverage for common profiles.
- Expand mapping for additional SKUs as fleet evolves (e.g., H200 or provider-specific variants).
comments: 2026-01-10 (Talia Benson): Creating as a standalone ticket because kernel selector v2 needs a stable GPU key; current name-based matching is duplicated in 3 places and breaks under MIG.
2026-01-21 (Yuki Sato): Drafted normalization contract. Plan is NVML-first, CUDA fallback. Will ensure selector sees only {sku_class, sm, is_mig, mig_profile_bucket}.

2026-01-29 (Yuki Sato): Implemented initial mapping rules for L4/A10/A100/H100 and Unknown. Added MIG detection via NVML; CUDA-only detection marks is_mig but doesn’t attempt profile parsing unless obvious.

2026-02-05 (Grace Kim): Review: please ensure we never emit raw device names into metrics. Also, compute capability should be surfaced even for Unknown GPUs for debugging; keep it as sm_<..> label (bounded set).
2026-02-08 (Thomas Baird): Cardinality review: OK to label `gpu_sku_class` + `gpu_sm` + `gpu_is_mig`. Not OK to include memory size as exact value; use coarse buckets if needed.

2026-02-12 (Yuki Sato): Hooked into selector context. Added tests for common device-name strings from fleet and a synthetic MIG fixture. Unknown path returns sku_class=Unknown and selector will fall back to safe set.
2026-02-18 (Connor O'Brien): Marking done for runtime-1.19 train. Ensure release notes mention improved GPU normalization for selector v2 diagnostics (no customer-facing change).
